ShortDescription.Value: Ski resorts: lifts that fit your terrain, runs on natural or machine-made snow, lodges, ski school and patrol, a resort planner, resort economics, and merging your own buildings.

Publish.LongDescription:
[Trailer](https://youtu.be/NJvzaxwGfa4) | [Features](https://youtu.be/mkysRTD0zmQ)
**Build a ski resort in Cities: Skylines II.**
Draw chairlifts, gondolas and an aerial tram up your mountain, draw runs down it, and natural or artificial snow will open the runs. Guests ski (simulated, not visualized, yet), buy tickets and lessons, and the resort draws tourists to your city. No mods required, but Anarchy and Move It are highly recommended, along with Write Everywhere.
## Highlights - **Four lifts, one tool.** Fixed-grip triple chairlift, detachable quad chairlift, gondola and aerial tram. Click the base station, click the top, and the tool plans numbered towers over your terrain. Chairs and cabins ride the rope. You can edit the tower placement. - **Runs on real snow.** Draw a run and set its features: groomed or natural, snow guns, floodlights for night skiing. Cat tracks and narrow ski ways link runs across the hill. Each run is rated from its hardest pitch, in North American or European grading. It opens at 3 ft (91 cm) of snow on 60 % of the run. Snow guns extend the season where it is cold enough. - **Resort Planner.** Outline a mountainside and get a plan of linked runs, cat tracks and lifts. Leave out what you do not want, then build it. - **Seasons.** Snow melts in spring, runs close and lifts stop. Lodges and the school close off-season. The aerial tram keeps running as summer sightseeing. Northern and Southern Hemisphere seasons are both accounted for. - **Lodges, Ski School and Ski Patrol.** Five lodges, a school and two patrol buildings, adding amenities (and costs) to your resort. - **Merge your own buildings.** Is there an asset you'd love to be in your ski area? A landmark, signature or recreation building near the runs can merge into the resort, increasing its attraction (and costs). - **Ski Bus Depot.** A coach stop in town that brings guests to a ski resort too far away for them to reach on their own. (Helps alleviate vanilla issues with travel times to far-away ski areas.) - **One hub.** The Ski Resort button (default top left) opens Attraction, Runs, Lifts, Guests, Finances and History views. You can also see any issues with your resort. - **A resort economy.** Lift tickets, season passes, lessons, lodge spend and running costs. A ski area's attraction score feeds the game's tourism, so a bigger resort brings more visitors.
## Requirements Cities: Skylines II 1.6 (tested on 1.6.4f1). No DLC or other mod required.
## Getting started 1. Open the Ski Resort hub. Place a Welcome Sign, then place a lodge near where the runs will be. 2. Pick a lift type. Place the base station, top station, then draw the line between them. Press Enter to build. 3. Connect a low-voltage power line to the base station. 4. Draw runs downhill from the top station, and wait for snow.
## Good to know - Skiers are counted, not visually simulated. Chairs and cabins move but carry no riders. (Post Park Adventures, I will try my best to at least get Cims on the chairlifts) - Ground: the Welcome Sign, the Ski Bus Depot, the A-Frame and Grand lodges and the tram base level their ground. Most chairlift and gondola stations cut a level pad. The other lodges, both patrol buildings, the Ski School and the fixed-grip and tram top stations are meant to be built into the hillside with the terrain tools or Move It. The Ski School is the most demanding: level the top of its magic-carpet area, then slope it down to the base. - Bulldozing a Welcome Sign also deletes every run linked to it, with the runs' glade trees, and refunds no run fee. There is a warning popup before you bulldoze the sign. - The Resort Planner is on by default. Its switch is in Options. - Options set the run grading (North American or European), the units, and slopes in degrees or percent. By default they follow the city's theme and the game's units. - Lifts can cross lifts of another type, over or under, where the towers can reach the height. Two lifts of the same type cannot cross. - A cat track cannot pass under a lift that is already built: build cat tracks first. - Lifts are power-line networks and need low-voltage power at the base station. The game refuses a city high-voltage line at a lift. This is an odd quirk of how I decided to build the lifts system. - Before uninstalling, use the "Delete all ski resort content" button in the mod's Options, then save the city. - Resorts cost money all year and earn in winter. Build in steps if budget-constrained. Welcome to ski resort economics!
## Guides and details - [Docs site](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort): guides, every number, settings and troubleshooting. - Start with the [Resort Quickstart](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/quickstart/) and the [Lifts guide](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/guides/lifts/). - Bug reports: the [Paradox forum thread](https://forum.paradoxplaza.com/forum/threads/modular-ski-resort.1949673/) or the [Discord thread](https://discord.com/channels/263634513861541888/1570379334672326736). Paste the text from the Copy diagnostics button in the mod's Options. - [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/theotherwildcathighboy/ModularSkiResort)
## Credits - Modular Golf Course Pack by joergeske: the modular recreation idea this mod grew from. - Meapy's Tourism Overhaul: studied for how tourism and attractions work. Not required. Works alongside this mod. - Logo and in-game icon by [Lexa](https://lexakeenen.com/). - All assets (chairs, lodges, patrol huts) are based on [real places](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/credits/#asset-inspirations). - Built with Claude (Anthropic) for decompilation, prefab work and asset generation. Direction and many, many hours of testing by the author. - [Full credits and licenses](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/credits/).
Publish.ChangeLog:
**Saves:** - Lifts, runs, cat tracks and resort buildings built from now on remember the version that built them, so a later update can bring older ones up to date. - A city saved with 1.0.2 still loads in 1.0.1, but that version forgets which version built what.
**Sync resort:** - When an update changes how resort objects should look, the hub's Overview shows "Sync resort" with the objects of that ski area that are out of date. The first one: Patrol Huts placed before 1.0.1 get their firewood pile. - Each object can be skipped or kept as it is. Sync is free and has no undo.
